samples.summary: copyThread detaches the anchor with detachYorkieValue, which this same PR documents as mangling nested Yorkie array proxies — corrupting `docs-range.posRange` and `pdf-text.rects` in every comments API response
samples.evidence: `comment-ops.ts:99` does `anchor: (detachYorkieValue(t.anchor) ?? {}) as AnyAnchor`. The doc block this PR adds to `yorkie-json.ts:13-20` states outright: "The obvious last resort — detachYorkieValue — is wrong ... it branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so a chart's `seriesColumns` or a slide's `elements` would come back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata." Two of the three anchor shapes this controller explicitly supports contain arrays: `frontend/src/types/comments.ts:31` `posRange: TreePosStructRange` (a pair), and `:69` `rects: PdfRect[]`. The editor's own stores go out of their way here — `docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-87` ("posRange is deliberately left as-is ... does not round-trip through JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))") and `files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:61` (`Array.from(anchor.rects ?? []).map(copyRect)`). Since `copyThread` backs `GET /comments`, `POST :threadId/replies` and `PATCH :threadId`, listing threads on a `doc` or a PDF text thread returns an anchor whose array field is CRDT metadata rather than the positions/rectangles — exactly the case the controller advertises as supported ("Listing, replying, resolving and deleting its threads are supported", comments.controller.ts:287). Worse, `detachYorkieValue` recurses via `Object.entries`, so if the CRDTArray exposes its internal node list the walk could recurse into circular RGA links. Every unit test in `comment-ops.spec.ts` uses plain-object fixtures, so nothing exercises the proxy path.

samples.summary: deleteThread returns 404 'Comment not found' for a thread with an empty comments array, making such a thread permanently undeletable through the API
samples.evidence: `deleteThread`'s authorize callback computes `rootCommentId(thread)` (`comments.controller.ts:613-615`), which is `copyThread(thread).comments[0]?.id` — `undefined` when the list is empty. `assertCommentAuthor` (line 527) then evaluates `commentId ? findComment(...) : undefined` → `undefined` → `throw new NotFoundException('Comment not found')` at line 528. A thread with zero comments should still be deletable (or at least not report the thread's own comment as missing); as written the only way to clear it is out-of-band CRDT surgery.

samples.summary: applySlideChange can call moveAfterByIndex(-1, from) when an array exposes moveAfterByIndex/getElementByIndex but not moveFront
samples.evidence: `slide-ops.ts:118-125`: the outer guard only requires `moveAfterByIndex && getElementByIndex`, but the head case at line 119 additionally requires `moveFront`. If a movable array lacks `moveFront`, a move to index 0 (`to === 0`, `to < from`) falls through to the `else` at line 123-124 and calls `moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)` = `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)`, an out-of-range index the Yorkie SDK will reject. The frontend equivalent (`yorkie-slides-store.ts:831`) branches on `clamped === 0` unconditionally, without the extra `&& moveFront` predicate.

samples.summary: An unknown --layout silently produces a slide built from the first built-in layout instead of a 400
samples.evidence: `slides.controller.ts:100` accepts any non-empty string as `layoutId` and hands it to `addSlide`, which goes through `MemSlidesStore.resolveLayout` (`packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:172-173`): `this.doc.layouts.find(...) ?? getLayout(layoutId)`, and `getLayout` (`packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198`) is `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(...) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]`. A typo'd layout id therefore reports HTTP 200 with `{id, index, slideCount}` for a slide that has a completely different layout — the `layouts` catalog this controller adds exists precisely so `layoutId` is checkable, but nothing checks it.

samples.summary: parseRef-based A1 validation accepts lowercase references and silently resolves them to a wildly wrong column
samples.evidence: `worksheet-images.ts:46-51` validates the anchor with `parseRef(anchor)` and stores the string verbatim on success. `parseRef` (`packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:341-347`) computes the column as `char.charCodeAt(0) - 65 + 1` with no case normalisation and no A-Z range check, so `"b2"` parses as column 34 rather than 2 and passes validation. The same helper backs `sheetCellAnchor` in `comments.controller.ts:649`, so `comments add ... --ref b2` either anchors the thread on column 34 or is refused with the misleading "has no stable row/column id yet" message.

samples.summary: addSlide emits an index-anchored insert while the module's own concurrency rationale is that changes carry ids, so a concurrent insert lands the new slide at the wrong position
samples.evidence: `slide-ops.ts` documents `SlideChange` as "resolved against the live array at apply time (`insert-after` / `remove` / `move` carry ids, not indices, so a concurrent insert elsewhere in the deck cannot make them land on the wrong slide)", but `addSlide` (line ~181) returns `{ kind: 'insert', slide, index: at }` where `at` was computed from the *pre-read* deck. `applySlideChange`'s `insert` case (line 97-101) only clamps against the live length, so a peer insert committed between the read and the write shifts the requested position by one. `duplicateSlide` avoids this with `insert-after`; `addSlide` with an explicit `--index` does not.

samples.summary: deleteSlide's last-slide refusal is decided on a stale read, so a concurrent delete can leave the deck with zero slides
samples.evidence: `deleteSlide` checks `doc.slides.length <= 1` on the document read *before* `doc.update` opens (`slides.controller.ts:150-155` calls `op(readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot()))` and only then enters `doc.update`). `applySlideChange`'s `remove` case (`slide-ops.ts:108-112`) re-resolves by id and splices unconditionally, with no re-check of the invariant. Two concurrent deletes on a two-slide deck therefore both pass the guard and produce the empty deck the guard exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. comment-ops.ts:99 does route the anchor through detachYorkieValue, and yorkie-json.ts:172 branches on Array.isArray, which this repository repeatedly documents as false for a Yorkie array proxy (yorkie-json.ts:13-20, worksheet-charts.controller.ts:58-66, yorkie-json.spec.ts:155-162, and the lessons file). Two supported anchor shapes carry arrays: docs-range posRange (types/comments.ts:31, written as a Yorkie array at yorkie-comment-store.ts:180-187, whose own comment at :81-87 says it must be left as-is) and pdf-text rects (types/comments.ts:69, written by text-selection.ts:198). The path is live: yorkie.service.ts:36-57 attaches a real yorkie.Document so doc.getRoot() yields proxies, and copyThread backs GET /comments (comments.controller.ts:253), mutateThread for replies and resolve (comments.controller.ts:599), plus findComment/rootCommentId. No guard sanitizes the anchor — isThread only checks comments, and withSref only rewrites sheet-cell anchors. So a docs thread's posRange and a pdf-text thread's rects come back as CRDT metadata instead of positions/rectangles on exactly the routes the controller advertises as supported. Wrong data on a normal path = major under the correctness rubric; the pdf-region case survives only because its nested rect is an object proxy, which is why the plain-object fixtures never catch it.
